question: An engineer needs to connect Cisco UCS Fabric Interconnect (FI) to an external storage array. Due to budget limitations, the engineer must connect a Cisco UCS FI directly to an FC storage port. Which two actions must be taken to complete this connection? (Choose two.)
options: Configure the fabric interconnect in end-host mode.
Create the required VSAN in the SAN cloud.
Set FC zoning to disabled when creating the VSAN.
Configure the fabric interconnect in FC switch mode.
theory: To directly attach an FC storage array's port to a fabric interconnect (bypassing an external SAN switch/MDS), the fabric interconnect must first be switched out of default end-host mode into FC switch mode, since only switch mode allows FC storage ports and native FC switching behavior. Because there's no upstream SAN fabric performing zoning in this direct-attach scenario, a storage connection policy must also be created on the UCS side to define the target WWPNs and zoning relationship between the server's vHBAs and the storage array. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS Storage Management, Direct-Attached Storage and FC Switch Mode)
